submission.implementation_notes: Revision 2 of the scenario (thread token): one script that runs as a minting policy for the token and as a spending validator for the funds, and reads its own hash from the script context. Written in `do`-notation on `Plinth.Validator`, an early-termination monad, together with the typed decoding DSL `Plinth.Decoder.Named`: each `ScriptContext` field is decoded with a single `Constr` walk, and a value that is only compared is never structurally decoded (`Plinth.Encoded`). The validator finds the escrow output with a module-local unique lookup and reads ADA with `assetAmount`. Compiled with Plinth 1.45.0.0; the validator is the one of `Plinth_1.64.0.0_Unisay`, carried to this line as a patch. This line has no inliner budget pragma. Its build configuration does not strip traces, so the artifact keeps the rule names that the validator passes to `traceError`, as the revision 1 artifact kept its messages. The plain implementation of this line is `Plinth_1.45.0.0_Unisay_plain`. Source: `lib/TwoPartyEscrow/Monadic.hs` (+ `lib/Plinth/Validator.hs`, `lib/Plinth/Decoder/Named.hs`, `lib/Plinth/Decoder/Named/ScriptContext.hs`, `lib/Plinth/Encoded.hs`) in plinth-cape-submissions @ 20cabddfa17709e759c6bd15f42e7ac1d6447047.
